builds.howItPlays: You empower your other units and spells, and each time you do, Mel becomes empowered too without costing you anything extra. Right before a fight, you spend that empowered state to shrink an enemy unit by two might, turning what looked like a losing fight into one you win.
builds.whyYou: You like picking apart your opponent's plans instead of overpowering them. You're comfortable holding cards back and waiting for the moment your shrink effect turns a bad fight into a good one. If it satisfies you more to out-think someone than to out-muscle them, Mel is a good fit.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 3.5: skillshotzgaming.com rates Mel's speed 'Moderate,' and riftboundguide.com describes a deck that spends its early turns on removal and unit development rather than racing. stance 2.5: riftboundguide.com calls Mel 'reactive rather than aggressive,' built around 'shrinking the opponent's unit before combat resolves' and holding spells like Rebuttal or Shock Blast for the opponent's response. complexity 6: riftboundguide.com says the Empower loop 'reads like a riddle' at first and 'once it clicks it is one of the more satisfying control engines,' while skillshotzgaming.com rates complexity 'Medium.' variance 2.5: riftboundguide.com notes 'the more Empower sources you play, the more consistently her loop fires,' so deck construction, not luck, drives reliability. Legend ability: whenever you empower something else, Mel becomes empowered too; exhausting her while empowered gives an enemy unit -2 might for the turn. Confidence: medium. Sources disagree on the archetype label (riftboundguide.com says Control, skillshotzgaming.com says 'Tempo/Control,' an earlier riftbound.gg summary leaned midrange); went with Control since two of three call it that and its reactive, low-variance shape fits the Control end of the scale. Reviewer should double-check the archetype call.
